office_does: The District 7 councilmember is one of seven Pierce County Council members who adopt the county budget, ordinances, taxes and land-use rules for Gig Harbor, Fox Island, the Key Peninsula and parts of north and west Tacoma.
race_blurb: An open seat between Democrat Brenda Lykins, a nurse practitioner and former Gig Harbor councilmember who took 56.9% in the primary, and Republican Mike Solan, a Seattle police officer and former police-guild president who took 29.2%. Both call for more deputies; they split over the county's 0.1% public-safety sales tax, spending, sheriff oversight and land-use regulation.

candidates.summary: Neonatal nurse practitioner, former Gig Harbor councilmember and Charter Review commissioner running on public safety, road and broadband investment, urban-focused housing and environmental protection.
highlights: Supports the 0.1% public safety sales tax to fund deputy 'recruitment, retention, and training' [S9]
Pairs sheriff staffing with mental-health responders and pushed for a sheriff-oversight ombuds charter amendment [S6][S14]
Would prioritize public safety, broadband, road maintenance and affordable housing while protecting the environment [S15]
Backs the Comprehensive Plan's shrinking of the rural growth area and urban, infrastructure-served housing [S6][S9]

taxes.basis: Supports the council-imposed 0.1% public safety sales tax as a stable, dedicated revenue source, in two separate interviews; a flat sales tax, not progressive revenue.

housing.basis: Names affordable housing as a priority but her stated tools are growth management (urban-focused growth, a smaller rural growth area, cottage housing) rather than deregulation or public housing and tenant protections.

safety.basis: Backs more deputies and the sales tax for 'a stronger law enforcement presence' and says she voted to increase Gig Harbor police staffing, while also pushing mental-health responders, violence prevention and a sheriff-oversight ombuds.

climate.basis: Prioritizes shoreline, forest and habitat protection and calls it an investment in climate resilience.

experience.basis: Former Gig Harbor councilmember and mayor pro tem now on the Charter Review Commission, running for an open seat.

candidates.summary: 27-year Seattle police officer and former Seattle Police Officers Guild president running on deputy staffing, fiscal accountability and less land-use regulation.
highlights: Would recruit and retain deputies and negotiate a new deputies' contract from 2027 [S2][S5]
Opposes the 0.1% public safety sales tax as written and passed without a public vote [S5]
Says county government 'spends too much money and has not budgeted within its means' and promises 'fiscal accountability' [S5][S11]
Opposes the sheriff-oversight ombuds as 'activist led' and an appointed sheriff [S10]
Endorsed by the Pierce County Deputy Sheriffs' Independent Guild, the Tacoma Police Union and the county Republican Party [S4]

taxes.basis: Opposes the public safety sales tax as passed without a public vote and calls for action on 'double-layered taxes', but says he would have backed a tax limited to law enforcement.

spending.basis: Repeatedly says the county spends too much and must live within its budget; pledges program reviews, an 'emergency audit', mandates-first funding and 'fiscal accountability'.

housing.basis: Says county regulation stifles growth and would cut red tape for a predictable land-use process and 'reasonable growth standards', while voicing support for parks and open-space conservation.

safety.basis: Centers his campaign on deputy recruitment, staffing and retention and opposes the sheriff-oversight ombuds; stated positions cover staffing and oversight only.

experience.basis: First run for office, saying he is 'not a career politician', though he brings 27 years in policing and six as guild president.
